dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation

evidence.note: Reads the template, lists data shards, runs nvidia-smi; identifies data format (263MB train / 576KB val .bin), vocab size 8192, tokenizer path, and hardware before writing the script — targeted environment orientation.

Proactively derives that the int8 quantized save would include both tied embedding and lm_head weights and would exceed 32MB, and fixes it before the first validation — a genuine size↔quantization design derivation up front.

Runs explicit contract verification: imports train_AGENT.py, loads via load_model_for_verification, checks forward logits shape and the cross_entropy loss contract, and measures quantized-checkpoint bpb — mapping the actual grader load/forward interface rather than assuming.
Decodes validation bytes/token to convert val loss to bpb, probing the real tokenizer/data to validate the pass threshold rather than guessing the conversion.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read the spec and template early, correctly identified data-shard format, vocab size 8192, the 32MB cap, and one loading path (clearing level 5), then deliberately mapped the full contract — load_model_for_verification, forward shape, int8 dequant round-trip, and loss = cross_entropy — while probing actual data and tokenizer for bytes/token (level 8). It stops short of 10: it implements only one load path, never explicitly reasons about bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB, or position-dependence of logits, and its deepest contract checks were performed late rather than fully front-loaded.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition

evidence.note: After minimal recon, agent immediately wrote a full 31.27M-param model (at the size ceiling) and launched an 8000-iteration run — no tiny end-to-end baseline first; capacity fixed at max from the start.

Proactively fixed the tied-embedding/lm_head size issue 'before training reaches a validation checkpoint' — shows implicit awareness of the size gate, but woven into the single big run rather than a separate milestone.
First checkpoint save + 28.9MB size confirmation happened at the iter-200 val interval, incidental to the big run rather than a deliberate 'verify save/size under budget' phase before scaling.
Grader-interface load, forward/loss-contract, and local bpb were verified only at the END of the full run — correctness not locked before capacity investment; bpb came out 0.98343, above target.
Reactive low-LR resume and bigram/trigram add-ons after the borderline result — improvement was iterative firefighting, not pre-planned ordered milestones with fallback branches.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed implicit ordering (train, save/quantize, then verify) and some size forethought, with continuous val/size monitoring, but never built a small end-to-end pipeline first and only verified the load/forward contract at the very end — so scaling and correctness were entangled, matching the level-3 anchor ('implicit ordering but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria'). It falls short of level 5, which requires a deliberate small-model baseline verified for save/load/quantize/budget before improving.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification

evidence.note: At every validation checkpoint the agent tracked the compressed checkpoint size (~28.8MB), continuously confirming the 32MB byte cap rather than trusting it once.

Final verification script imports train_AGENT.py, loads the compressed checkpoint through load_model_for_verification (the grader's own entry point), checks file size, and validates the forward/loss contract — end-to-end through the actual interface.

Reloaded the quantized checkpoint and computed local bpb = 0.98343, recognized it exceeded 0.983, and resumed training. This demonstrates treating local val_bpb from the dequantized checkpoint as a calibrated proxy against the real threshold, and catching a near-miss before submission.

Re-verified after fine-tuning and bigram augmentation: reload via load_model_for_verification, loss contract satisfied, size 30.27MB under cap, local bpb 0.97891 — repeated the full contract+size+bpb check as the plan/checkpoint changed.
Repeatedly reasoned that the ~0.004 local margin was small relative to the stated ~0.05 hidden/local bpb variance, showing explicit awareness of proxy noise and desire for threshold margin.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification), reloads the quantized checkpoint to confirm int8 dequant round-trips and compute local bpb, checks the loss contract, tracks size against the 32MB cap throughout, and explicitly treats local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin awareness against 0.983 — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because it tested only one of the two load paths, never asserted logits depend on position or ran a shifted-pass bpb harness, and verification was a manual final-stage gate rather than an automated regression harness run every iteration.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking

evidence.note: Evaluated validation loss at every 200-iteration checkpoint (4.464 → 2.6396), continuously comparing against an estimated bpb target and converting loss via bytes/token; watched for divergence/plateau — noting at steps 39-41 the curve had 'nearly plateaued but still marginally improving.'

Ran final quantized verification and measured actual local bpb = 0.98343, ABOVE the 0.983 threshold — detected the run was borderline/failing despite good nat-loss, then decided to resume low-LR fine-tuning rather than submit.

Monitored resume run every 100 iters, saved only improvements, and repeatedly reasoned about margin under proxy noise ('margin only ~0.004 bpb, smaller than the stated hidden/local variation'), an explicit near-threshold-under-noise done-vs-remaining read.

Recognized diminishing returns from fine-tuning and deliberately reallocated remaining checkpoint headroom to bigram then trigram residual augmentation, abandoning the trigram when it failed to improve rather than grinding a saturated config.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent tracked the val proxy against the target across the entire arc, distinguished plateau, and made continue/stop/change decisions based on that read (level 8), and further showed level-10-flavored behavior: explicit near-threshold-margin-under-proxy-noise reasoning and deliberate reallocation to fine-tuning and n-gram augmentation. It falls short of a clean 10 because during the long main run it relied on estimated bytes/token conversions rather than measured bpb (only computing real bpb at the end) and let the fixed 8000-step schedule grind through an evident plateau. That places it solidly at 8.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints

evidence.note: Diagnosed the torch.compile crash (missing C compiler) and disabled compile via COMPILE=0, and preemptively fixed a checkpoint size overshoot by removing duplicated tied lm_head weights — cause-directed corrections, not blind tweaks.

Final quantized bpb (0.98343) came in ABOVE the 0.983 target; agent recognized the miss, diagnosed it as a borderline quant-loss problem, and launched a targeted low-LR resume fine-tune (RESUME=1, LR=0.0002) saving only on improvement — a reasoned single-lever change with re-check.
Used the ~3.16MB byte-budget headroom to add a sparse bigram residual bias table to buy accuracy within the size cap — trading spare capacity against the byte budget, the level-8 behavior.
Tried a trigram residual table, found no improvement, abandoned it and restored the valid bigram checkpoint — killing a dead-end early rather than sinking more compute.

The main training run was a single fixed 31M-param, 8000-iter run monitored passively; no architectural/sizing experimentation, and corrections bought only marginal bpb with a thin final margin (0.979 vs 0.983) despite noted hidden-split variance — falls short of frontier-level headroom optimization.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly diagnosed the binding constraints at each failure point (compile crash, size duplication, borderline quantized bpb) and adapted the right lever: low-LR resume fine-tuning for quant loss and a bigram residual using leftover byte headroom to buy accuracy within the cap — matching the level-8 'trade capacity against the byte cap' behavior, and it abandoned the trigram dead-end early. However, the corrections produced only tiny compounding gains, the core architecture was never re-explored, and the final margin stayed thin without achieving real headroom, keeping it below the level-10 'frontier as object of optimization.' This places it solidly between the 5 (single reasoned lever) and 8 (binding-constraint diagnosis with design adaptation) anchors.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation

evidence.note: Went straight from writing the full script to launching a large main run (initially 6000 then 8000 iters), with no cheap end-to-end validation pass reserved first; the model was deliberately sized to ~31.27M params to fill the 32MB budget (capacity roughly sized to the goal), but iteration count/batch were picked without any probe or payoff reasoning.

Across dozens of steps the agent simply lets the single 8000-iter cosine run proceed, repeatedly saying 'continue', spending whatever the run takes with no comparison of expected payoff across alternative uses of compute — hallmark of implicit budget spending.

Only after the full run finished did it discover local bpb ~0.98343, just above threshold, then reactively launched a 3000-iter low-LR fine-tune phase — an unplanned extra phase triggered by the borderline result rather than pre-allocated.

Further reactive spend: added bigram then trigram residual tables using leftover checkpoint headroom to squeeze margin; this is post-hoc reaction to a thin margin, not upfront cross-phase allocation or evidence-based sizing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implicitly spent whatever its main run took and passively monitored it (anchor 3), but it did roughly size model capacity to the byte/goal budget and reactively added fine-tuning/augmentation phases when the result came in borderline. It never reserved cheap compute for a baseline/contract validation pass before the long run, and ran no probes to estimate the steps/capacity needed to cross the threshold, so it falls short of anchor 5's baseline-first reservation and well short of the explicit phase allocation of 8. This places it between anchors 3 and 5, at a 4.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train an LM on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit an int8-compressed checkpoint (≤32 MB decimal) that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty is multi-source: an exact and dual-path loading/forward contract that silently fails the grade if mismatched, a hard size budget coupled to model capacity via quantization, training convergence under implicit compute limits, and a local val_bpb proxy that must be trusted and monitored. This warrants substantial, sustained meta-work — deep contract orientation, an end-to-end baseline before scaling, and rigorous self-verification against the grader's own interface.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the loading/forward contract, data format (.bin shards, tokenizer), size budget, and template before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads via one of two specific interfaces and calls forward with two exact signatures; a checkpoint that trains perfectly but violates the contract or size cap scores zero. Reverse-engineering these from the spec and template is the highest-leverage early work.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no reading of the template, data format, tokenizer, or the loading/forward contract; assumes defaults.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; aware there is a size limit and a val target but hazy on the exact load path or the dual forward signature.
anchors.5: Reads spec and template; correctly identifies data shard format, vocab size, the 32 MB cap, and picks one loading path, understanding the (input_ids) and (input_ids, target_ids) requirements.
anchors.8: Deliberately maps the full contract: which load function the grader uses, what shape/type it returns, how int8 dequant must round-trip, that logits must depend on position and loss must equal cross_entropy of those logits; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Also anticipates edge cases in the contract (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB) and derives the size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope up front, turning orientation into concrete constraints that shape every later decision.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered milestones — a working end-to-end pipeline before scaling — each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Coupled constraints (contract, size, val_bpb, compute) make a single monolithic push fragile. Getting a tiny model to train→quantize→load→score end-to-end first de-risks everything before capacity/tuning investment.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: launch a big training run hoping it trains, fits, loads, and passes all at once.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (train, then quantize, then submit) but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria; scaling and correctness entangled.
anchors.5: Clear phases: get a small model training, verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, measure baseline val_bpb, then improve — with rough success criteria per phase.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete gate (loads via grader interface / size < 32MB / forward contract holds / val_bpb measured), sequenced so contract+size correctness is locked before capacity scaling and tuning.
anchors.10: Milestone structure explicitly manages the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off as ordered decisions with fallback branches, so each subsequent run is a targeted step on a known frontier rather than a fresh gamble.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond training loss: that the checkpoint loads via the grader's own interface, fits the byte cap, satisfies both forward signatures, and dequantizes correctly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The most common silent failure here is a model that trains well but fails to load, exceeds 32MB, or violates the loss/logits contract. Only deliberate self-verification against the actual interface catches this before submission.

anchors.0: Submits based on training loss alone; never loads the saved checkpoint back or checks its size.
anchors.3: Checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.
anchors.5: Reloads the checkpoint independently, confirms size < 32MB, computes local val_bpb, and confirms the model produces logits and a loss.
anchors.8: Verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification or GPT+dequantize), asserts the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, that logits depend on position, and that int8 dequant round-trips — treating the local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
anchors.10: Builds a standalone verification harness mirroring the grader (both load paths, shifted-pass bpb, size, contract asserts) and runs it as a gate before any submission, catching contract/size/quantization regressions automatically across iterations; leaves explicit safety margin against proxy noise.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb trajectory vs the target and of compute spent vs remaining, detecting divergence, overfitting, or plateaus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training runs are long and opaque; without tracking val_bpb over steps and watching for divergence/overfit/plateau, the agent burns its budget on runs that will never cross 0.983 or silently regress.

anchors.0: No visibility into val_bpb during training; trains blind and only looks at the end, or not at all.
anchors.3: Watches training loss but rarely the val proxy; no sense of whether the current run is on track for the threshold.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during/after runs and compares to the 0.983 target, noticing gross problems like divergence or no improvement.
anchors.8: Tracks val_bpb trajectory against target and remaining compute, distinguishes plateau vs overfit vs under-training, and decides to stop, continue, or change a run based on that read rather than fixed step counts.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate done-vs-remaining model across many runs — recognizing diminishing returns, near-threshold margins under proxy noise, and thrash — and reallocates effort deliberately instead of grinding a saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, quantization, hyperparameters, or plan when a run diverges, overshoots the size cap, or fails to approach the target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts routinely miss on size or bpb; progress depends on diagnosing WHY (too big, under-capacity, bad LR, quant loss) and changing the right lever rather than repeating the same run.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or ignores a size/contract failure and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected tweaks (nudge LR, shrink randomly) without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: On a clear miss (over budget, diverging, plateaued above target) makes a reasoned single-lever change — e.g. adjust dims to fit, change LR, tune training length — and re-checks.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the binding constraint from evidence (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization vs size) and adapts the design accordingly, e.g. trading depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap.
anchors.10: Treats the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization: uses each falsified run to update the design model and make principled, compounding corrections that move toward the threshold with headroom, abandoning dead-end approaches early rather than sinking further compute.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation
dimensions.description: Deciding how to spend limited training compute/wall-clock across baseline validation, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning.
dimensions.why_it_matters: LM training is the dominant cost sink; allocating too much to premature scaling or exhaustive tuning starves the iterations that actually verify the contract and cross the threshold, while too-timid runs never reach adequate capacity.

anchors.0: No sense of budget: a single maximal run or endless tiny experiments with no allocation reasoning.
anchors.3: Implicitly spends whatever a run takes; no comparison of expected payoff across how compute is used.
anchors.5: Reserves cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before committing to a longer training run, and roughly sizes runs to the goal.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget across phases — cheap end-to-end validation, a right-sized main run, targeted tuning — and adjusts allocation as results come in.
anchors.10: Runs small, informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, then invests the main budget on that evidence, reserving margin for a final verified submission rather than over- or under-spending.
